page_title: Tokenized Money Market Funds — Digital Assets Dashboard
page_subtitle_html: Tokenized money market fund (MMF) exposure aggregated from RWA.xyz US Treasuries and Non-U.S. Government Debt. Networks and platforms are built from each fund's on-chain token deployments; Distributed Value columns are current levels.
kpi_window_note: Distributed value uses a 30-day (30D) % change vs summed token values 30 days ago. Top network share is the largest network by distributed value; the 30D figure is the change in market-share percentage points (pp), not a percent of total. Fund universe: fixed curated TMMF population on RWA.xyz US Treasuries and Non-U.S. Government Debt; KPIs, charts, and league tables use the same fund set.
key_observations_html:
Key observations

  • TMMF distributed value fell 7.9% over 30D: With distributed value at $12.39B (7.9% lower over 30D). Related: Securitize, Ethena Open BUIDL Facility With $100M Capacity (The Defiant).
  • Early "flight to efficiency" shows up in TMMF 30D network share: Among tokenized money market funds, gainers include Stellar (+7.41% 30D TMMF network share), Solana (+2.48% 30D TMMF network share); losers include Ethereum (-10.21% 30D TMMF network share), Avalanche C-Chain (-0.95% 30D TMMF network share). That pattern is consistent with TMMF issuers routing more distributed value toward higher-throughput, lower-fee chains—though Ethereum still dominates TMMF share levels in most snapshots.
  • Multi-chain footprints are a distribution signal: Funds listing many networks with thin holder counts usually signal jurisdictional or distribution reach, not deep secondary liquidity on every chain. Related: Bitcoin ETFs shed $2.35B in 2 weeks, BlackRock’s losing streak hits 11 (CoinTelegraph).
  • Rates still matter as much as product and chain choice: Rate and money-market moves can reshape fund-level inflows as quickly as any chain or product launch story. Related: Live updates: Bitcoin eyes bear market lows as late summer rally mostly wiped out (CoinDesk).
  • A global regulatory arbitrage map is emerging: distributed value clusters into distinct compliance regimes—U.S. Reg S ~36% of population AUM (e.g. USDY, USYC); U.S. Reg D ~34% of population AUM (e.g. iBENJI, BUIDL); U.S. mutual fund (N-1A) ~6% of population AUM (e.g. WTGXX, FILQ-A). Issuers appear to anchor products in familiar safe harbors rather than one global standard. Related: Microsoft confirms global outage resolved, rules out cyberattack (CoinTelegraph).

Context only—not investment advice. Observations rank fund-level and network aggregates on this page against recent tokenization and money-market headlines. Bullets combine on-page data with recent industry headlines.

Key observations are AI generated and should be reviewed for accuracy.
